The governor made the declaration during an interview with select journalists in Benin City, where he spoke on his administration’s achievements, security measures and efforts to improve residents’ welfare. Okpebholo said he was prepared to sign the death warrant of anyone convicted of kidnapping, irrespective of their relationship with him, insisting that even if the convict were his father, he would approve the execution. He disclosed that he had contacted the state Attorney-General to inquire about the necessary documents for executing some convicted kidnappers. However, he said the convicts had appealed their sentences, adding that his administration would continue to pursue the cases through the judicial process. “I will sign the death warrant, even if it is my father, I will sign it, if i see this paper today now, i will sign it and i will even supervise the killing, we won’t just leave them to go like that. We will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. we will not spare anybody,” he said. The governor also defended his administration’s security measures, including the demolition of buildings allegedly used by criminals, saying the actions had helped reduce cult-related killings and restore nightlife and business activities in parts of the state. On infrastructure, Okpebholo said his administration was executing road construction projects, rehabilitating schools and improving healthcare facilities across the state. He cited ongoing projects in previously neglected communities, including the road linking Auchi, Ewu and Ekpoma. The governor said his administration was focused on practical governance and prudent management of public resources, adding that he wanted to be remembered for his achievements rather than the amount of money accumulated while in office. He maintained that fulfilling his promises to Edo residents and ensuring that development reached communities across the state remained his administration’s priority.
